paragraphs.text: An animated companion that shows live DSH agent progress in the macOS notch.
DSH Notch Pet
Your DSH agent, living at the top of the screen.

On macOS it tucks into the MacBook notch. On Windows it floats at the top
center of the primary disp

lay. Either way it shows the current session, the
exact step the agent is on, and how far the turn h

as come — without opening a
window.

DSH Notch Pet shows the session title and the live step line that DSH shows in
the chat. Hover and i

t unfolds into a compact status card with elapsed turn
time, task or goal progress, the session's to

ken usage, the active-agent count,
the model, and one-click access back to DSH.

## What it looks like

*macOS, collapsed: the title and live step sit beside the notch, with a progress
hairline underneath
. It never adds height to the strip.*

*macOS, expanded: up to two title lines, live step, elapsed time, `Tasks 3/7`,
active agents, the se

ssion's token usage and cache hit, the goal, the model, and
the controls.*
## Highlights

- **Live, not decorative.** The line under the title mirrors the step DSH shows
below the assistant

message: a changing reasoning preview while the model
thinks, `Editing file · native/Sources/PetView

.swift` while a tool runs, and
elapsed turn time on the right. It deliberately avoids the finished a

ssistant
reply.
- **Progress without invented percentages.** It uses `todo_write` completion when
DS

H has tasks, and falls back to goal rounds when it does not. With no
countable unit, the bar shimmer

s indeterminately while the agent works, then
freezes or disappears when it stops.
- **The session's

bill, not a guess.** The expanded footer reads the same
provider-reported `tokenUsage` projection a

s DSH's own Usage pill: cumulative
billed input plus output, with the cache-hit share beside it. No

estimator and
no extra model calls.
- **Gets out of the way.** Turn on **Only while working** and th

e panel is ordered
out entirely whenever no task is running. A pawprint takes its place in the
menu

bar or system tray; on macOS a second switch hides that too. Pinning
overrides it. Prefer a quieter

top edge? **Hide pet** drops the animated mascot
and its glow while keeping the session title, live

step, progress, and token
readout.
- **Six accents, honest status colors.** Glacier (the default cya

n), Aurora,
Iris, Sakura, Tangerine, and Mint, plus a custom hue/saturation/brightness
picker. Waiti

ng stays amber, errors stay red, and completed turns stay mint.
- **At home on both platforms.** mac

OS uses a nonactivating AppKit/SwiftUI panel
with no Dock icon; Windows uses a nonactivating WPF win

dow with no taskbar
button, per-monitor DPI scaling, Reduce Motion support, and the same 60 fps
prog

ress animation. Neither steals focus.
- **Bilingual without a restart.** The interface follows the m

acOS or Windows
display language by default and falls back to English for every other locale.
**Sett

ings → Language** switches between Follow system, English, and 中文, and
the panel, menu, and settings

update immediately.
- **Local by design.** The host talks to the panel over a private Unix socket o

mediately.

## Requirements

- **macOS 14 Sonoma or newer**, or **Windows 10 (1809 or newer) / Windows 11**
with .NET Framework 4

.8. Current Windows 10 and Windows 11 releases include
4.8; Windows Update can install it if a machi

ne is missing it.
- DSH Desktop, or a DSH host running inside a macOS or Windows GUI session.
- The

bundled helpers are prebuilt: an ad-hoc-signed universal binary for macOS
and a .NET Framework execu

table for Windows. Nothing is compiled on install.
- Xcode Command Line Tools only if you rebuild th

e macOS helper; PowerShell and
the in-box .NET Framework compiler only if you rebuild the Windows he

OS helper; PowerShell and
the in-box .NET Framework compiler only if you rebuild the Windows helper.

A notched MacBook is not required: on other Macs the panel floats at the top
center of the main disp

lay with rounded top corners. Windows PCs have no
hardware notch, so they always use that rounded-to

d top corners. Windows PCs have no
hardware notch, so they always use that rounded-top presentation.

## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The host half is shared and platform-neutral above the transport layer. It
builds a single snapshot

from DSH's own services and events, so the two helpers
render the same data model. The Windows helpe

r is a native WPF overlay compiled
against .NET Framework 4.8; it does not require Electron, a brows

er, or a
developer SDK at install time. It is nonactivating, has no taskbar button, sits
above norma
l windows, and uses per-monitor DPI scaling.
## Privacy

Everything stays on your computer. On macOS the host writes the current state to
a per-process Unix

socket (`0600`) under
`~/Library/Application Support/DSHNotchPet/`, and the panel reads it. On Windo

ws
the state goes to a per-user named pipe and, when no pipe client is attached, to
a user-local sna

pshot under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DSHNotchPet\`. The plugin makes no network
calls, collects no telemetry,

and needs no account. The Windows fallback exists
for managed environments that deny named-pipe cli

ents; it never leaves the
user's profile.
Logs are local too:

- macOS: `~/Library/Logs/DSHNotchPet.log` and `DSHNotchPet-host.log`
- Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DSHN

otchPet\logs\DSHNotchPet.log` and
`DSHNotchPet-host.log`
